newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland ready to receive Yugoslavia war criminals.
newsitem.headline: Finland ready to receive Yugoslavia war criminals.

text.p: Finland is ready to make space in its jails for convicted war criminals from the former Yugoslavia, Finnish media reported on Friday.
Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen formalised the offer by signing an agreement with the United Nations war crimes tribunal in The Hague on Wednesday, the national news agency STT said.

Italy has already made a similar agreement and other European countries are expected to sign such accords soon, STT said. Finnish radio said Finland would be the first country where an agreement would take force.
STT quoted a foreign ministry official as saying that the first convicted war criminals could arrive in Finland late this year.
Finland does not intend to accept leading political war criminals requiring exceptionally high-security jails.
The two most prominent indicted suspects are former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and former Bosnian Serb military commander General Ratko Mladic, both of whom remain at large.
The Hague tribunal on Wednesday found Bosnian Serb Dusan Tadic guilty of war crimes and crimes against humanity for his part in a Serb "ethnic cleansing" campaign against Bosnian Moslems in 1992.
The judgment was the first in a full-length trial since the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia was set up by the U.N. Security Council in May 1993.
It is the first international body for the prosecution of war crimes since the Nuremberg and Tokyo trials held in the aftermath of World War Two.
Tadic, one of eight war crimes suspects held at the tribunal's detention centre, has already spent more than three years in custody. He faces a maximum sentence of life imprisonment.
